newsitem.title: USA: Foreign crude offers swelling US Gulf with supply.
newsitem.headline: Foreign crude offers swelling US Gulf with supply.

text.p: Foreign crude offerings in the U.S. Gulf continued to swell on Friday, with refiners getting tastes of a variety of grades for April delivery.
"There are lots of people out their trying to sell Brent, but not many people taking it," said a Texas trader.
Talk in the market pointed to more Brent on the way, with Swiss traders Glencore currently said to be loading an Ultra Large Crude Carrier for April delivery to the Gulf.
Still, traders said the most popular sweet grades were seen on offer from West Africa.
"A lot of people have been buying West African, Bonny's and some Forcados are still out there, too," said a source.
Price ranges saw Brent talked for April 20-30 delivery at May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus 75 cts on a delivered basis to the U.S. Gulf.
Forcados was offered at Dated Brent plus $1.75 for the same period, traders said.
On the South American front, Oriente traders in the U.S. Gulf said the market was stilted all week.
"We're really waiting for prices from Ecuador before things start moving," said a trader.
Most Oriente was said to be placed for April under previous commitments, at prices around May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus $1.05-$1.10.
